title: Borel Localization for Compact Torus Actions

items.title: Fixed loci and normal weights of compact torus actions
items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $r\geq 0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ with its product Lie-group structure, and let $M$ be a compact, finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Let $a:T\times M\to M$ be a jointly smooth left action. Then $M$ admits a smooth Riemannian metric invariant under $a$. Its fixed set
$$
F=M^T:=\{p\in M:a(t,p)=p\text{ for every }t\in T\}
$$
is a compact embedded smooth submanifold with finitely many connected components, and $T_pF=(T_pM)^T$ for each $p\in F$. The orthogonal normal bundle $\nu_F=(TF)^\perp\subset TM|_F$ has no nonzero $T$-fixed vectors in any fiber. On each connected component of $F$, its normal representation has a finite weight decomposition into nontrivial characters of $T$, with constant multiplicities; equivalently, $\nu_F$ admits a smooth $T$-invariant complex structure and orientation on each component.

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and R. Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 3, fixed-point and normal-representation discussion, printed pp. 7–9.

references.title: Shubham Dwivedi, Jonathan Herman, Lisa C. Jeffrey, and Theo van den Hurk, Hamiltonian Group Actions and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 9.9, Example 9.48, PDF pp. 85–86.

items.title: Equivariant tubular and slice neighborhoods for compact torus actions
items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, and let $g$ be a $T$-invariant Riemannian metric. If $S\subseteq M$ is a compact embedded $T$-invariant submanifold, its orthogonal normal bundle $
u(S)$ has a $T$-invariant open disk neighborhood $D_\epsilon(
u(S))$ of the zero section, and the normal exponential map is a $T$-equivariant diffeomorphism from that disk bundle onto a $T$-invariant open neighborhood of $S$. In particular, for $x\in M$, with stabilizer $H=T_x$, orbit $O=T\cdot x$, and normal fiber $V=
u_x(O)$, let $H$ act on $V$ by its differentials. There is an open $H$-invariant disk $D_\epsilon(V)$ such that $[t,v]$, the equivalence class of $(t,v)$ under $(t,v)\sim(th,h^{-1}v)$ for $h\in H$, maps by $[t,v]\mapsto t\cdot\exp_x(v)$ to a $T$-equivariant diffeomorphism from $T	imes_H D_\epsilon(V)$ onto an open neighborhood $U_x$ of $O$. Every stabilizer of a point in $U_x$ is a subgroup of $H$.

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and R. Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 3, orbit tubes and isotropy groups, printed pp. 6–8.

items.title: A proper closed subgroup of a torus has a nonzero annihilating character
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ with $r\geq1$, and let $H\subsetneq T$ be a closed subgroup. A character means a smooth group homomorphism from $T$ to the multiplicative unit circle $S^1=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$. Then there is a nontrivial character $\chi:T\to S^1$ whose restriction to all of $H$ is the trivial character.

references.locator: Section 3, isotropy-subgroup support, printed pp. 6–8.

items.title: Localization preserves exact sequences of modules
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity, let $S\subseteq R$ contain $1$, be closed under multiplication, and not contain $0$, and let $0\to M'\xrightarrow{f}M\xrightarrow{g}M''\to0$ be an exact sequence of $R$-modules. The localization $S^{-1}M$ is the module of fractions $m/s$, with $(m,s)\sim(m',s')$ exactly when some $t\in S$ satisfies $t(s'm-sm')=0$. Then
$$
0\longrightarrow S^{-1}M'\xrightarrow{S^{-1}f}S^{-1}M\xrightarrow{S^{-1}g}S^{-1}M''\longrightarrow0
$$
is exact.

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and R. Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 3, localization of equivariant-cohomology modules, printed pp. 5–7.

items.title: Rational coefficient ring and characters of a product torus classifying space
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $r\geq0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$, and use $E_T=(E_{S^1})^r$, the product of the right Milnor join models, with $BT=E_T/T$. For the $i$th coordinate character $\chi_i([t_1,\ldots,t_r])=\exp(2\pi i t_i)$, let $L_i=E_T\times_T\mathbb C_{\chi_i}$ be the associated complex line bundle over $BT$, with the right diagonal equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi_i(t)^{-1}z)$, and put $u_i=c_1(L_i)\in H^2(BT;\mathbb Q)$. Then
$$
BT\cong(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r,\qquad H^*(BT;\mathbb Q)\cong\mathbb Q[u_1,\ldots,u_r],\qquad |u_i|=2.
$$
Every smooth character $\chi:T\to S^1$ is uniquely $\chi_{\mathbf n}([t])=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i n_it_i)$ for $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb Z^r$, and its associated line satisfies $c_1(L_{\chi_{\mathbf n}})=\sum_i n_i u_i$. In particular a nontrivial character has a nonzero degree-two class. For each $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, $H_q(BT;k)$ is finite-dimensional in every degree $q$. For $r=0$, $BT$ is a point and its rational cohomology is $\mathbb Q$.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Section 3.2, Theorem 3.19, printed pp. 220–222.

items.title: Homotopy invariance of singular cohomology with field coefficients
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be topological spaces, and let $f,g:X\to Y$ be continuous maps joined by a continuous homotopy $H:X\times[0,1]\to Y$. Then $f^*=g^*:H^n(Y;k)\to H^n(X;k)$ for every integer $n$. Consequently every homotopy equivalence induces an isomorphism on singular cohomology with coefficients in $k$.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §3.1, Induced Homomorphisms and Homotopy Invariance, printed p. 201 (chapter PDF p. 17): dualization of the prism chain homotopy. The local proof records field coefficients and zero/negative-degree conventions explicitly.

items.title: A compact smooth manifold has a finite good-cover nerve model
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $F$ be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary and equip it with a Riemannian metric. An open set is strongly geodesically convex if every ordered pair of its points is joined by a unique affinely parametrized globally length-minimizing geodesic whose image stays in the set and whose connector depends smoothly on the endpoints. There are finitely many such open sets $U_1,\ldots,U_N$ covering $F$, every nonempty finite intersection of which is strongly geodesically convex. Let $K$ be the finite simplicial complex whose nonempty faces are the index sets $\sigma\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ for which $U_\sigma=\bigcap_{i\in\sigma}U_i$ is nonempty. Then its usual geometric realization $|K|$ is homotopy equivalent to $F$. For $F=\varnothing$, take $N=0$ and $K=\varnothing$.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §4.G, Propositions 4G.1–4G.2 and Corollary 4G.3, printed pp. 458–459 (chapter PDF pp. 38–39): a paracompact good cover has the homotopy type of its nerve. Strong convexity and its finite-intersection property are the separately declared local mathematical supplier, not an extra hypothesis extracted from this citation.

items.title: Positive-degree cohomology of a compact manifold is nilpotent
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $F$ be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, equipped with a Riemannian metric, and let $k$ be a field. There is a finite CW complex $K$ homotopy equivalent to $F$, and an integer $N\geq1$ such that $H^q(F;k)=0$ for every $q\geq N$. Consequently the ideal $J=\bigoplus_{q>0}H^q(F;k)$ in the graded cohomology ring satisfies $J^N=0$. If $F=\varnothing$, take $K=\varnothing$, $N=1$, and $J=0$.

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and R. Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 3, finite-dimensional cohomological support argument, printed pp. 6–9.

items.title: The fixed-locus Borel base is paracompact and of CW type
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $r\geq0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ use the product Milnor model $BT=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$ with its ordinary product topology, and let $F$ be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Then $BT\times F$ is paracompact Hausdorff and has the homotopy type of a CW complex. In fact, there is a finite CW complex $K$ such that $BT\times F\simeq BT\times K$.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Vector Bundles and K-Theory
references.locator: Appendix “Paracompactness,” Propositions 1.18 and 1.20, printed pp. 35–37.

references.locator: Appendix, Theorem A.6 on products of CW complexes, printed pp. 524–525.

items.title: Character localization in Borel equivariant cohomology
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ and use the product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$, $BT=ET/T$, with right diagonal action $(e,x)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)$. For $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, put $A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k)\cong k[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, where $u_i=c_1(L_{\chi_i})$ is the degree-two class of the $i$th coordinate character line. For a smooth character $\chi:T\to S^1$, set $L_\chi=ET\times_T\mathbb C_\chi$, with the right equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)$. If $\chi=\chi_{\mathbf n}$ for $\mathbf n\in\mathbb Z^r$, then $c_1(L_\chi)=\sum_i n_i u_i$. Define $\mathscr S_T(k)$ to consist of $1$ and all finite products of $c_1(L_\chi)$ for nontrivial characters $\chi$. This is a multiplicative subset of $A_T(k)$ with $0\notin\mathscr S_T(k)$. For a topological space $X$ with a continuous left $T$-action, set $H_T^*(X;k)=H^*(ET\times_T X;k)$, with its $A_T(k)$-module structure induced by $ET\times_T X\to BT$. For an $A_T(k)$-module $N$, its localization $\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}N$ consists of fractions $n/s$, with $n\in N$, $s\in\mathscr S_T(k)$, and $n/s=n'/s'$ exactly when $u(s'n-sn')=0$ for some $u\in\mathscr S_T(k)$; addition is $(n/s)+(n'/s')=(s'n+sn')/(ss')$, and scalar multiplication is induced by the localized ring. The character-localized Borel equivariant cohomology is $\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(X;k)$. For $r=0$, there are no nontrivial characters and $\mathscr S_T(k)=\{1\}$.

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and R. Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 3, localization of equivariant-cohomology modules, printed pp. 5–7.

references.title: Shubham Dwivedi, Jonathan Herman, Lisa C. Jeffrey, and Theo van den Hurk, Hamiltonian Group Actions and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 9.10, Borel localization theorem and localized modules, PDF pp. 86–87.

items.title: The fixed normal equivariant Euler class is a localized unit
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, and set $F=M^T$. Give the normal bundle $
u_F=(TF)^\perp$ the componentwise $T$-invariant complex orientation supplied by the fixed-locus normal-weight decomposition. Let $
u_{F,T}=ET	imes_T
u_F	o BT	imes F$ be its Borel vector bundle and let $e_T(
u_F)\in H_T^*(F;k)=H^*(BT	imes F;k)$, $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, be its zero-section Euler class. Then $e_T(
u_F)$ is a unit in $\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(F;k)$. On each connected component $F_0\subseteq F$, restriction to $BT	imes\{p\}$, $p\in F_0$, is the product of the nontrivial character classes of the normal representation at $p$, with multiplicity and the chosen complex orientation.

references.locator: Section 3, equation (3.7) and its normal-weight derivation, printed pp. 8–9.

items.title: Equivariant cohomology of the nonfixed locus vanishes after character localization
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable manifold $M$ without boundary, let $F=M^T$, and use the product Milnor Borel construction with coefficients $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$. Let $\mathscr S_T(k)$ be the multiplicative set generated by the first Chern classes of all nontrivial smooth characters of $T$. Then
$$
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(M\setminus F;k)=0.
$$
Equivalently, every class in the Borel equivariant cohomology of the nonfixed locus is annihilated by some finite product of nontrivial character classes.

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and R. Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 3, orbit-isotropy support and finite cover argument, printed pp. 5–8.

references.title: Shubham Dwivedi, Jonathan Herman, Lisa C. Jeffrey, and Theo van den Hurk, Hamiltonian Group Actions and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 9.10, proof of Theorem 9.50, PDF pp. 86–87.

items.title: Borel localization for compact torus actions
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, and let $F=M^T$. For $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, define $H_T^*(X;k)=H^*(ET\times_T X;k)$ using the product of the right Milnor circle models, let $A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k)$, and let $\mathscr S_T(k)$ be the multiplicative set generated by the first Chern classes of all nontrivial smooth characters $T\to S^1$. Then restriction along $i:F\hookrightarrow M$ induces a graded-ring isomorphism
$$
i^*:\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(M;k)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(F;k).
$$
The conclusion concerns compact finite-dimensional smooth $T$-manifolds and ordinary Borel singular cohomology; it makes no noncompact or compact-support assertion.

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and R. Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 3, Theorem 3.5 and equation (3.7), printed pp. 8–9.

references.title: Shubham Dwivedi, Jonathan Herman, Lisa C. Jeffrey, and Theo van den Hurk, Hamiltonian Group Actions and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 9.10, Theorem 9.50 and proof, PDF pp. 86–87.

title: Borel Localization for Compact Torus Actions — Examples

items.title: Circle rotation on the complex projective line
items.statement:
Let $T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ act on $M=\mathbb{CP}^1$ by $t\cdot[z_0:z_1]=[z_0:e^{2\pi it}z_1]$. For $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, use the product Milnor Borel model and let $u=c_1(L_\chi)\in H^2(BT;k)$ for $\chi(t)=e^{2\pi it}$. The fixed set is $F=\{p_+,p_-\}$, where $p_+=[1:0]$ and $p_-=[0:1]$; the tangent weights are $+1$ at $p_+$ and $-1$ at $p_-$. If $\mathscr S_T(k)$ is generated by nontrivial character classes and $A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k)$, then restriction identifies
$$
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(\mathbb{CP}^1;k)\cong \mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k)\oplus\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k),
$$
with the two summands given by evaluation at $p_+$ and $p_-$.

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and R. Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 3, fixed-point restriction and normal weights, printed pp. 7–9.

items.title: A free circle orbit has zero localized Borel cohomology
items.statement: Let $T=M=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ act on $M$ by left translation $t\cdot[x]=[t+x]$, and use the product Milnor Borel model with $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$. This action has no fixed point. The map $[e,x]\mapsto e\cdot x$ identifies $ET\times_TT$ with $ET$, so $H_T^*(T;k)\cong k$ in degree zero and is zero in positive degrees. Every positive-degree class in $A_T(k)$ acts as zero, so localization at the nontrivial character classes gives $\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(T;k)=0$, agreeing with restriction to the empty fixed set.

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and R. Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Section 3, orbit-isotropy support, printed pp. 5–8.

items.title: Rotation on one factor of a product with positive-dimensional fixed components
items.statement:
Let $T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ act on $M=\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$ by $t\cdot([z_0:z_1],q)=([z_0:e^{2\pi it}z_1],q)$, and let $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$. The fixed set is the disjoint union $F=(\{p_+\}\times\mathbb{CP}^1)\amalg(\{p_-\}\times\mathbb{CP}^1)$, with $p_+=[1:0]$ and $p_-=[0:1]$; the normal weights are $+1$ and $-1$, respectively. Let $u\in H^2(BT;k)$ be the weight-one character class and $b\in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1;k)$ the generator with $b^2=0$. Then localized restriction identifies
$$
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(M;k)\cong \bigl(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k)\otimes_k k[b]/(b^2)\bigr)\oplus \bigl(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k)\otimes_k k[b]/(b^2)\bigr),
$$
where the two summands are the Borel cohomology of the two positive-dimensional fixed components.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Section 3.2, Theorem 3.19, printed pp. 220–222.
